correctness.rationale: The published classification reduces polymorphism-homogeneity to a precise functional-digraph condition. The species recurrence follows from the unique cycle-plus-in-trees decomposition. The overlap correction by permutations is exact, the height sum is coefficientwise finite, and the asymptotic is controlled by the unique simple pole of 1/(1-z exp(z)); a uniform radius 0.58 bounds all higher-height strata. Exhaustive maps through seven points and an independent formal-series calculation through ten points agree.

value.rationale: The result converts a qualitative classification into an exact labeled census and a sharp asymptotic. It identifies a natural dominant mechanism—source height one—and proves all higher common heights are exponentially smaller. This quantitative refinement is reusable for comparing homogeneity properties across finite unary algebras and is not merely a small-order table.
